title: Bolstered bloc of Vermont Republicans see bills repealed this year as a win
why: Vermont’s enlarged Republican minority is claiming victory this session not for laws it passed but for measures it rolled back, a shift that signals growing GOP leverage in a state long dominated by Democrats.

title: China resumes US soybean purchases under trade deal with Trump, but future for farmers remains ‘daunting’
why: China — the biggest buyer of American soybeans — is placing orders again after a new trade deal, but volumes remain far below pre-trade-war levels, leaving Mississippi and Midwest growers financially exposed heading into harvest.

title: Aspen Acres fire grows to 87,000 acres as firefighting force expands on Fourth of July holiday
why: The Aspen Acres fire nearly doubled to about 87,000 acres over the holiday — one of five major Colorado wildfires burning nearly 180,000 acres combined — as crews expanded and officials urged residents to skip fireworks amid widening evacuations.

title: This summer’s ‘dead zone’ in the Gulf will be larger than average
why: NOAA forecasts a low-oxygen ‘dead zone’ topping 7,000 square miles this summer, driven by Mississippi River nutrient pollution that suffocates marine life and squeezes fisheries across the Gulf Coast.

title: ‘A self-inflicted tragedy’: Congress approves reversal of US climate policy
why: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act — signed into law July 4 — sunsets the Inflation Reduction Act’s clean-energy tax credits, gutting the only federal climate strategy and stranding wind and solar projects nationwide unless they break ground within days.

title: ‘This is My Country Now’: 52 new citizens naturalized on Long Island before July 4
why: At a Long Island ceremony, 52 immigrants became U.S. citizens just before July 4 — a snapshot of the naturalization path continuing even as the Supreme Court’s TPS ruling and stepped-up enforcement unsettle immigrant communities.

title: The days are hot, but so are the nights. That’s a problem, experts say
why: As a heat dome bakes up to 90 million Americans, LPM examines how rising overnight temperatures rob bodies of recovery time — a mounting public-health risk that makes heat waves deadlier, especially for people without air conditioning.

title: State budget revisions save Santa Clara County from deeper cuts
why: California’s newly signed budget delivers $900 million for homeless services — nearly double Gov. Newsom’s proposal — while preserving in-home care and mobile mental-health teams and delaying some Medi-Cal cuts for immigrants, sparing Santa Clara County from the deepest reductions.

title: What, to the Immigrant, Is Your Fourth of July?
why: On the nation’s 250th birthday, currently and formerly detained immigrants describe what citizenship and belonging mean amid intensified ICE enforcement — first-person reporting that reframes the holiday from inside the immigration system.

title: Texas Stock Exchange to launch trading Monday
why: Backed by BlackRock and Citadel Securities, the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange begins a phased launch this week — the best-funded challenge to the NYSE–Nasdaq duopoly in decades, with major stocks set to trade by month’s end.

title: Colorado’s wildfires scorch 129,000 acres as critical fire danger persists
why: Six large wildfires have burned more than 200 square miles across Colorado, with the Aspen Acres fire alone destroying as many as 200 structures and forcing widening evacuations as hot, dry, windy weather offers little relief.

title: Appeals court says undocumented immigrants must get bond hearings
why: The 5th Circuit ruled the government can’t detain undocumented immigrants indefinitely without a bond hearing, rejecting a Trump administration policy and potentially affecting thousands held in detention across Texas and beyond.

title: 5 people sue Border Patrol agents over use of tear gas, unlawful detention during Midway Blitz
why: Five Chicagoans allege Border Patrol agents tear-gassed and unlawfully detained them during an immigration operation on the Southwest Side — among the first lawsuits to challenge the tactics used in the city’s “Midway Blitz” enforcement surge.

title: Senatobia police stonewall requests for details of officer shooting that killed 1-year-old outside Walmart
why: Weeks after an officer shot and killed 1-year-old Kohen Wiley during a shoplifting call, Senatobia police are withholding basic records about the shooting, testing Mississippi’s public-records law amid mounting demands for accountability.

title: State budget will defund IOLTA, leaving many poor North Carolinians without civil legal support
why: North Carolina’s budget strips funding from the account that bankrolls civil legal aid, threatening representation for the state’s poorest residents in eviction, domestic-violence and benefits cases — a cut other states could copy.

title: Workforce Pell is here. States are racing to catch up.
why: A new federal program lets low-income students use Pell grants for short-term job training for the first time, but uneven state readiness means many of the roughly 100,000 students expected to benefit each year won’t see aid for months or years.

title: NY budget lets Hochul spend $1.5B without normal oversight
why: Lawmakers quietly exempted nearly $1.5 billion from the state comptroller’s contract review in the new budget, letting Gov. Hochul’s administration sign deals without the watchdog scrutiny normally required — a rollback of a key anti-corruption check.

title: Danger Behind Bars: Mississippi keeps sending suicidal prisoners to solitary
why: Nearly 50 people have died by suicide in Mississippi’s solitary-confinement units since 2015, yet the state keeps isolating vulnerable prisoners despite evidence the practice deepens mental illness — a joint investigation with Mississippi Today and the Clarion Ledger.

title: UPS didn’t require inspection of part that failed before deadly Louisville crash
why: UPS never required the detailed inspections that could have caught the engine-mount failure blamed for a crash that killed 15 people last fall — raising hard questions about maintenance oversight at one of the nation’s largest air-cargo carriers.

title: Congressional Black Caucus hit by Supreme Court ruling
why: A Supreme Court decision weakening the tools used to draw majority-Black districts threatens the political clout of the Congressional Black Caucus, with ripple effects for minority representation in Connecticut and states nationwide.

title: ‘This has become a national fight’: Aspen Acres fire expands, scorching 35,000 acres
why: The wind-driven Aspen Acres fire has burned 35,000 acres and destroyed more than 180 structures across Pueblo and Custer counties, forcing an out-of-state incident team to take command as evacuations widen.

title: Officer who shot baby Kohen Wiley in Senatobia was not in harm’s way, family attorney says
why: An independent autopsy presented by attorney Ben Crump contradicts the police account of a Senatobia officer who shot and killed a 1-year-old, intensifying scrutiny of the shooting and demands for accountability.

title: La Tuna federal prison in Anthony to close, ending nearly a century of operations
why: The Bureau of Prisons will shutter the 94-year-old La Tuna complex, eliminating hundreds of local jobs as part of a nationwide closure push driven by aging infrastructure and staffing shortages.

title: New Britain to sue Erin Stewart after missed repayment deadline
why: New Britain’s mayor is suing his predecessor, former mayor Erin Stewart, to recover more than $100,000 tied to how she improperly boosted her own pay over 12 years — a notable municipal accountability case.

title: Days After Supreme Court TPS Ruling, Little Haiti Wonders What’s Next
why: After the Supreme Court cleared the way for the administration to end Temporary Protected Status, roughly 330,000 Haitians nationwide face deportation; Documented captures the fear gripping Brooklyn’s Little Haiti.

title: DeKalb Rejects Data Center Regulations, but Fight Continues
why: DeKalb County commissioners voted down proposed data center rules after a year of resident pushback, a decision that tests how majority-Black communities can shape the fast-growing industry reshaping neighborhoods nationwide.

title: As Montana’s Medicaid work requirements loom, questions about system gaps remain
why: Montana is among the first states to impose Medicaid work requirements, and reporting reveals unresolved system gaps that could cost eligible low-income residents their coverage — a preview for the many states following suit.

title: On the upper Texas coast, many petrochemical facilities may not be prepared for fiercer storms
why: A Tribune investigation finds many Gulf Coast petrochemical plants — sources of toxic releases during past hurricanes — remain underprepared for stronger storms, exposing nearby communities to chemical hazards as climate-driven weather intensifies.

title: Jefferson County Clerk, state elections officials offer dueling takes on ballot errors
why: Following an LPM investigation into misassigned ballots, the county clerk and state officials clash over blame, and the clerk now seeks funding to audit precinct assignments for nearly 600,000 addresses before the next election.

title: DACA Recipients Detained, Deported by Trump Administration
why: The Trump administration has begun detaining and deporting DACA recipients despite polling showing broad public support for protecting them — a major escalation that puts roughly 500,000 “Dreamers” at risk of removal.

title: Phil Weiser beats U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet in Colorado’s Democratic primary for governor
why: Attorney General Phil Weiser knocked off sitting U.S. Sen. Michael Bennet in the governor’s primary, and 29-year-old democratic socialist Melat Kiros ousted longtime Rep. Diana DeGette — a night of insurgent upsets that signals how far the party’s energy has shifted from its establishment.

title: Utah’s massive Cottonwood Fire has already destroyed more than 100 structures, cost over $20M
why: The wind-driven Cottonwood Fire has leveled more than 100 structures and run up a $20 million firefighting bill, with families waiting days to learn whether their cabins survived — the latest sign of how a drought-stricken West is entering an explosive and costly fire season.

title: Order restored after hours-long hostage standoff inside ENC regional detention center
why: An hours-long hostage standoff at the Bertie-Martin Regional Detention Center in Windsor exposed the volatility inside a rural North Carolina jail that also holds immigration detainees, raising fresh questions about staffing and conditions at facilities far from public view.

title: 25 states sue Trump administration over Medicaid work requirements
why: Connecticut joined 24 other states and D.C. in suing to block new federal Medicaid work rules that health officials warn could strip coverage from hundreds of thousands of low-income adults — a fight whose outcome will decide who keeps their health insurance in dozens of states.

title: San Marcos becomes the first Texas city to ban data centers, testing its local control
why: San Marcos banned data centers within city limits, becoming a test case for whether local governments can keep the power-and-water-hungry facilities out — the same fight now playing out in West Virginia, Nashville, Kansas City and rural communities across the country.

title: Nearly 27,000 Mississippi college students may see state support shrink as aid programs face a shortfall
why: A funding shortfall in Mississippi’s financial aid programs could shrink grants for almost 27,000 students, and lawmakers say a fix may not come until 2027 — leaving low-income students in one of the nation’s poorest states uncertain whether they can afford to return in the fall.

title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump’s attempt to end birthright citizenship
why: On the final day of its term the Supreme Court, 6-3, upheld the 14th Amendment’s guarantee of citizenship for nearly all children born on U.S. soil, firmly rejecting Trump’s day-one executive order — a ruling that settles the status of millions of U.S.-born children of immigrants nationwide.

title: Who were the Midway Blitz Border Patrol agents? Most were veteran immigration officers
why: Block Club identified the Border Patrol agents who carried out Chicago’s aggressive “Midway Blitz” immigration sweeps, finding most were seasoned officers reassigned from the border — a rare look at who is actually conducting the interior raids reshaping immigrant neighborhoods.

title: Why is it so unusually expensive to replace lead pipes in Chicago?
why: Chicago says replacing each of its 400,000-plus lead service lines — the nation’s largest inventory — costs about $31,000, more than six times the EPA’s $4,700 national estimate, a cost gap that threatens to leave the poorest residents drinking from lead pipes long after federal deadlines pass.

title: Digging In: What happened as Louisville jail’s healthcare provider went bankrupt
why: An investigation traces how the private company paid to provide medical care inside Louisville’s jail slid into bankruptcy, leaving incarcerated people with gaps in treatment — a cautionary tale for the many jails that outsource inmate health care to for-profit vendors.

title: Tameshia Shelton freed after 11 years as appeals court finds her guilt was never proven
why: An appeals court freed Tameshia Shelton on her birthday after 11 years in prison, ruling prosecutors never proved her guilt beyond a reasonable doubt in a 2015 murder case — a wrongful-conviction reversal that spotlights how thin evidence can still send people to prison for life.

title: Ruling blocking Trump's SAVE system won't help Texas voters already flagged as noncitizens
why: A court blocked the Trump administration's use of the federal SAVE database to flag noncitizen voters, but Texans already wrongly marked for removal get no automatic relief — leaving thousands to prove their citizenship before they can cast a ballot.

title: Florida's 'Alligator Alcatraz' immigration detention center has closed, governor says
why: Florida's governor says the Everglades detention camp that became a national symbol of harsh immigration enforcement has closed and its detainees moved elsewhere, a reversal that reshapes scrutiny of the conditions migrants endured there.

title: Hinds County DA Jody Owens pleads guilty to federal conspiracy charge, will resign
why: The district attorney for Mississippi's largest county admitted to a federal conspiracy charge from an FBI public-corruption sting and will resign Wednesday, a stunning fall for Jackson's top prosecutor that upends who oversees criminal justice in the state capital.

title: Weekend flooding highlights persistent problems with Kentucky dam safety
why: Weekend flooding exposed how many of Kentucky's aging dams are privately owned and lack money for repairs or emergency plans, leaving downstream communities at risk as extreme rainfall grows more frequent.

title: ICE ramps up operations in Milwaukee while advocates rush to catch up
why: ICE arrested dozens of people across greater Milwaukee in a weekend 'targeted operation,' leaving immigrant families and legal advocates scrambling to locate detainees — part of an enforcement surge hitting Midwestern cities far from the southern border.

title: Officials identify three federal firefighters killed battling wind-driven Snyder Fire
why: Federal officials named the three Rifle Helitack crew members — two of them women in their 20s — killed as 100-mph winds drove the Snyder Fire across the Colorado-Utah line, underscoring the deadly conditions facing wildland crews as an explosive fire season grips the drought-stricken West.

title: One year later, Ohio professors say Senate Bill 1 changed how they teach and work
why: A year after Ohio's Senate Bill 1 banned most campus DEI work and stripped faculty strike rights, professors describe canceled programs, new civics mandates and self-censorship — a preview for the many states copying Ohio's higher-education overhaul.

title: Billionaire Jeff Yass pours $10 million into PAC backing Ohio governor candidate Vivek Ramaswamy
why: A single $10 million check from Pennsylvania investor Jeff Yass now bankrolls the main PAC behind GOP gubernatorial frontrunner Vivek Ramaswamy, a vivid example of how a handful of megadonors can dominate a statewide race — a dynamic playing out in governor's contests across the country.

title: Pennsylvania's fatal overdose prosecutions divide grieving families
why: Pennsylvania prosecutors increasingly charge those who supplied a fatal dose with drug-delivery-resulting-in-death, and the practice is splitting grieving families — some demand the charges, others say they jail fellow users instead of confronting addiction.

title: West Virginians won local control over landfills decades ago. Now they want it over data centers.
why: A new state law strips counties of zoning, noise and lighting authority over hyperscale data centers and routes most of the tax revenue to the state — echoing a 1980s fight over landfills and previewing the local-versus-state clashes erupting as the AI data-center boom lands in communities across the country.

title: Cherry and Iron wildfires top 71,000 acres as Utah towns evacuate again
why: Two wind-driven wildfires near Eureka and St. George burned past 71,000 combined acres, forcing repeat evacuations and prompting “last resort” power shut-offs that left towns dark — what Gov. Spencer Cox called some of the worst fire conditions in Utah’s history as the drought-stricken West heads into a dangerous summer.

title: 23,000 acres of Ohio public land up for fracking in upcoming votes
why: State officials are deciding whether to open roughly 23,000 acres of publicly owned wildlife areas, including Jockey Hollow and Egypt Valley, to oil-and-gas drilling — a high-stakes test of how much of Ohio’s public land gets leased to frackers over the objections of conservation groups.

title: Why New York’s ‘precision policing’ raises civil rights concerns
why: A close look at the NYPD’s data-driven “precision policing” shows how targeting small groups deemed likely to commit violence can sweep up people based on who they know rather than what they’ve done — a model spreading to other departments that advocates warn deepens surveillance of Black and Latino neighborhoods.

title: Florida’s notorious ‘Alligator Alcatraz’ immigration detention center is now closed
why: The remote Everglades detention camp that became a national symbol of harsh immigration enforcement has shut down, a reversal that changes where hundreds of detainees are held and sharpens scrutiny of the conditions migrants endured there.

title: Cornyn opposes Texas Republicans’ push to close GOP primaries
why: Sen. John Cornyn broke with Gov. Greg Abbott and AG Ken Paxton over a plan to bar independents from voting in Republican primaries, warning it would shrink the party — a fight over who gets to vote that is playing out in other one-party-dominated states.

title: Missoula delays security camera upgrade over AI surveillance concerns
why: The City Council held off on buying new park surveillance cameras after residents raised alarms about AI-powered facial recognition and tracking, opting to write a governing policy first — a local test of how cities set guardrails on surveillance tech before deploying it.

title: Wyoming designates its first-ever protected pronghorn migration corridor
why: Gov. Mark Gordon approved the nation’s first fully designated pronghorn migration route at the 6,000-year-old Trapper’s Point crossing, a precedent other Western states are likely to weigh as they try to balance energy and development against the big-game migrations their ecosystems depend on.

title: Haitian families brace for deportation after Supreme Court TPS ruling
why: After the Supreme Court let the administration end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians, families who have worked legally and built lives in the U.S. could lose their status overnight — a wrenching shift for hundreds of thousands of people and the communities and employers that rely on them.

title: Mississippi’s soaring prison rate could be curbed by a real public defender system, official says
why: Mississippi is among the few states with no statewide public defender system, and a state official argues that building one could ease one of the nation’s highest incarceration rates — a structural gap that keeps poor defendants jailed longer and that other underfunded states share.

title: DeWine vetoes bill requiring photo ID for mail voting in Ohio
why: Republican Gov. Mike DeWine vetoed a GOP-backed measure to require photo ID for absentee ballots, siding with seniors, disabled voters and students who rely on mail voting and setting up a clash with his own party over ballot access heading into the November election.

title: Former Mississippi state Sen. Philip Moran and son sentenced for bribery
why: Ex-state Sen. Philip Moran and his son, a former Diamondhead councilman, were sent to prison for bribery and conspiracy, a rare corruption conviction of a sitting-era Mississippi lawmaker that signals prosecutors’ willingness to pursue Gulf Coast political graft.

title: Glacier National Park employees vote to unionize
why: Workers at Glacier and 11 other National Park Service sites across the West voted 317-11 to unionize after the Trump administration’s deep Park Service cuts, a rare labor win on federal public lands that could give rangers leverage over staffing and safety as visitation peaks.

title: Judge blocks Tennessee mandate to report undocumented families seeking children’s care
why: A court temporarily blocked Tennessee from forcing doctors to report the immigration status of families using Children’s Special Services, a program for kids with serious medical needs — a fight over whether immigration enforcement can be wired into children’s health care that other states are watching.

title: Supreme Court ends protected status for thousands of CT Haitians
why: The U.S. Supreme Court let the Trump administration end Temporary Protected Status for roughly 1.3 million immigrants, including Haitians and Syrians, exposing longtime residents who have worked legally for years to sudden deportation — a ruling whose fallout will hit immigrant communities in every state, with Connecticut’s large Haitian population among the first to feel it.

title: Santa Clara County and state seek immediate halt to ICE facility
why: California’s attorney general and Santa Clara County asked a federal court to stop construction of a 150-bed immigration detention center near Gilroy, testing how far local and state governments can go to block ICE expansion on their own turf.

title: Supreme Court clears way for Trump to revive restrictive asylum policy
why: The justices cleared the path to reinstate “metering,” which caps how many migrants can seek asylum each day at the U.S.-Mexico border, a change that will quickly reshape conditions at El Paso and other crossings and could strand thousands of asylum seekers in Mexican border cities.

title: Utah’s Cottonwood Fire grows to 70,000 acres near Beaver
why: The fast-moving Cottonwood Fire ballooned to roughly 70,000 acres near Beaver, forcing evacuations and straining crews as an unusually dry, hot stretch primes the Intermountain West for a destructive wildfire season.

title: Mayor creates Gun Violence Reduction Office, but critics question its impact
why: Mayor Brandon Johnson signed an executive order creating an Office of Gun Violence Reduction as a step toward a permanent department, but anti-violence workers question whether a new bureaucracy will actually reach the neighborhoods hit hardest by shootings.

title: What 911 calls reveal about jails in St. Louis, Cleveland and Jackson
why: By obtaining 911 logs that local officials tried to keep secret, reporters documented surges of emergency calls — medical crises, suicide attempts, fires and assaults — that expose patterns of neglect inside three city jails, offering a replicable method other newsrooms can use to pierce jail secrecy nationwide.

title: Legislative committee probes Montana Lottery audit report
why: A state accountant told lawmakers the Montana Lottery’s books were off by $18.5 million over several years because its former financial-services director stopped doing his job before his 2025 death; auditors found no fraud but a breakdown of internal controls in an agency that funnels revenue to the state.

title: Families, patients of disabled Kentuckians demand renewed clinic funding at hearing
why: Kentuckians with intellectual and developmental disabilities packed a Frankfort hearing to fight cuts that will force the Lee Specialty Clinic to slash outpatient care in July, eliminating services for more than 1,000 of the state’s most medically vulnerable residents.

title: Mexican man dies in ICE custody in Laredo, at least the 20th fatality this year
why: A Mexican man died in ICE custody at a Laredo detention center — at least the 20th death in immigration detention nationwide this year and the fifth in Texas — intensifying scrutiny of medical care and oversight as ICE holds record numbers of detainees.

title: Final report on NES winter storm response cites flaws, suggests changes
why: An outside after-action report found Nashville Electric Service botched its response to a winter storm that knocked out power to half its customers, faulting emergency planning, public communication and crew coordination — and laying out fixes before the next disaster.

title: Utah officials warn of ‘totally unprecedented’ water shortages as towns run dry
why: Wells and streams are running dry and Utah towns face cutoffs as Lake Powell nears a record low and the seven Colorado River states stay deadlocked over how to share a shrinking supply — a water crisis rippling well beyond Utah across the entire basin.

title: Trump administration sues New York over its immigration package
why: The Trump administration sued New York over its new immigrant-protection laws, escalating a federal-versus-state showdown over sanctuary policies whose outcome could set precedent for how far Washington can force local cooperation with ICE.

title: Colorado won federal approval to import prescription drugs from Canada. Now comes the hard part.
why: After seven years of applications, Colorado won federal approval to import lower-cost prescription drugs from Canada — a first-in-the-nation green light that other states pursuing the same path will watch closely as a real-world test of whether importation can actually lower drug prices.

title: Ohio nursing home chain Arbors repeatedly accused of deadly neglect
why: At least 11 wrongful-death suits since 2024 accuse the Arbors at Ohio nursing-home chain of letting thin staffing cause the falls and bedsores that killed residents, a Signal Ohio review of thousands of court records found — exposing how chronic understaffing turns deadly in facilities caring for the frail elderly.

title: NY primary results: DSA set to pick up 6+ seats in Albany
why: Democratic Socialists are poised to gain at least six New York legislature seats after Tuesday’s primaries, prevailing despite a record $9.6 million in outside spending — nearly five times 2024 levels — a result that signals the left’s growing strength in Albany and offers a template other DSA campaigns will study.

title: Addicted to gambling in Illinois: ‘Someone has decided they can make money off you’
why: Block Club Chicago examines how Illinois’ embrace of legalized sports betting and casinos is fueling addiction, profiling residents who lost everything and tracing who profits — a cautionary case as states nationwide chase gambling tax revenue.

title: NY primary results: DSA set to pick up 6+ seats in Albany
why: Democratic Socialists are poised to gain at least six New York legislature seats after Tuesday’s primaries, winning despite an enormous wave of outside spending against them — a result that signals the left’s growing clout in Albany heading into November.

title: ICE and Greene County Sheriff’s deputies arrest numerous people in Ruckersville operation
why: ICE agents working alongside Greene County sheriff’s deputies arrested numerous people in a Ruckersville raid, a visible instance of local law enforcement openly assisting federal immigration operations that puts sheriff-ICE cooperation in rural Virginia under scrutiny.

title: Former CBI scientist Missy Woods pleads guilty in Colorado DNA evidence scandal
why: Former Colorado Bureau of Investigation forensic scientist Yvonne “Missy” Woods pleaded guilty to four felonies for mishandling DNA evidence, ending a scandal that cast doubt on more than 1,000 criminal cases and forced the state to re-examine convictions built on her work — a warning to crime labs everywhere about the fragility of forensic evidence.

title: Santa Clara County balances budget without severe service cuts
why: Santa Clara County closed a $787 million deficit and adopted a $14.7 billion budget without gutting services, preserving homelessness, suicide-prevention and public-health programs that other large counties are slashing amid similar shortfalls.

title: Colorado plan to ban using food assistance benefits for soda blocked by federal court
why: A federal judge ruled the USDA lacks authority to let states bar SNAP recipients from buying soda, blocking Colorado’s waiver and similar restrictions in several other states — a decision that reshapes what tens of millions of low-income Americans can buy with food benefits.

title: Report: CT schools among the most segregated in the U.S.
why: A new report ranks Connecticut sixth-worst for economic segregation and third-worst for ‘poverty packing’ in its schools, quantifying how district lines concentrate low-income students in one of the nation’s wealthiest states — a pattern other states draw on to challenge their own boundaries.

title: Most data centers ignore Texas surveys about their water use
why: Fewer than a third of Texas data centers answered a state survey on how much water they use to cool their servers, leaving regulators and the public blind to the strain on supplies as the AI build-out accelerates — the same transparency gap now fueling data-center fights in Ohio, Wisconsin and Mississippi.

title: Internal audit details financial oversight failures behind EPISD’s budget crisis
why: An internal audit found El Paso ISD’s former CFO and finance team knew for months that the district’s finances were deteriorating but failed to warn the superintendent or board, laying out the oversight failures behind a budget crisis now facing one of the region’s largest school systems.

title: Many Kentucky providers serving vulnerable patients brace for 4% Medicaid rate cut
why: Gov. Andy Beshear’s administration will cut Medicaid reimbursement rates 4% starting in August, squeezing hospitals, physicians and psychologists who treat Kentucky’s poorest patients and threatening access for the roughly 1.5 million Kentuckians on Medicaid.

title: Family seeks ways to honor Black WWII veteran killed by the KKK
why: After Wilkinson County supervisors refused to rename a road for a Black World War II veteran gunned down by the White Knights of the KKK, his family is looking for other ways to memorialize him — a reminder of how contested the public reckoning with racial violence remains in the Deep South.

title: Here's the latest on the Salt Lake City fire burning near the University of Utah
why: A fast-moving fire on Salt Lake City's eastern bench forced closures across the University of Utah campus and disrupted the Red Butte concert series, with crews racing to contain a blaze near densely populated neighborhoods at the height of fire season.

title: City Council names Rob Harrington next Charlotte mayor
why: Charlotte's City Council appointed attorney Rob Harrington to lead one of the nation's largest cities after Mayor Vi Lyles' surprise resignation seven months into a fifth term, handing an unelected newcomer the mayoralty of a major metro until the 2027 election.

title: San Jose Vietnamese community reeling following war memorial statue theft
why: Thieves tore the South Vietnamese soldier from San Jose's 'Thank You America' memorial, prompting the mayor and council to pledge a swift response and shaking a refugee community for whom the statue is a symbol of sacrifice and a shared U.S.-Vietnam history.

title: Extortion and pollution killed the data center bill
why: A once-popular Vermont data-center bill collapsed under a last-minute fee regulators opposed and an unresolved water-pollution loophole — a case study other statehouses are watching as they weigh the energy, water and environmental costs of the data-center boom now sweeping Ohio, West Virginia and Mississippi.

title: Jury finds broker Chad Banken preyed on Muslim homebuyers in contract-for-deed scheme
why: A Minnesota jury found real-estate broker Chad Banken liable for consumer fraud and discrimination for using contracts for deed to sell homes at inflated prices to Muslim buyers — a verdict that grew out of a 2022 Sahan Journal/ProPublica investigation and sets a marker for legal exposure over predatory home-sale schemes that target immigrant and faith communities nationwide.

title: Abu-Ali Abdur'Rahman, ex-Tennessee death row inmate, dies at 75
why: Abu-Ali Abdur'Rahman, whose death sentence Nashville's district attorney moved to vacate in 2019 over 'overt racial bias' in jury selection, died of liver cancer at Riverbend — closing a case that became a touchstone for challenges to racial discrimination in capital punishment.

title: Across Vermont, networks of volunteers push back on Trump's immigration enforcement
why: From verifying ICE sightings to tracking who has been detained, ordinary Vermonters are organizing rapid-response networks amid a climate of fear — a ground-level look at how rural communities are improvising oversight of intensified federal immigration operations.

title: In southeast Montana, a history of coal mining haunts farmers and ranchers
why: Ranchers along the Tongue River say decades of coal mining and methane drilling have pushed corrosive, sodium-laden water to the surface and helped wipe out fish in Montana's largest state water project — a multigenerational accountability story about extraction's lasting toll on rural livelihoods.

title: Colorado helium reserves got more valuable after war with Iran cut off 30% of the world's supply
why: With the Strait of Hormuz closed and Qatar's exports halted, Colorado — part of the world's largest helium field — has become strategically critical to a gas essential for MRIs, semiconductors and rockets, showing how a Mountain West resource is suddenly entangled in global conflict.

title: Despite state bans, abortions have almost doubled — the reason? Pills via telehealth
why: New data show abortions have nearly doubled even as more states enforce bans, driven by medication mailed through telehealth — concrete evidence that prohibition has reshaped rather than reduced access, with direct implications for every state now trying to police pills crossing its borders.

title: Trump wants to unleash 'America First' fishing. What's he really doing?
why: A Trump push to "unleash American fishing" would reopen protected marine areas and loosen catch limits, a deregulation drive that weighs a short-term commercial boost against the long-term collapse risk for fish stocks coastal states depend on.

title: In Utah, here's why some measles exposure sites never appear in public alerts
why: A review of more than 900 pages of state and local health records shows Utah officials quietly omitted many measles exposure sites from public alerts as cases climbed, leaving residents unaware they may have been exposed during a fast-growing outbreak.

title: Health insurers are seeking rate hikes again. Here's what to know
why: Connecticut insurers want average increases of 16.2% for individual plans and 17.8% for small-group plans covering roughly 220,000 people, previewing the kind of premium shock households in many states may face for 2027 coverage.

title: More Bible stories in public schools, changes to history lessons before Texas education board today
why: The State Board of Education is set to finalize a mandatory reading list that weaves in Bible stories while deemphasizing race and cultural diversity in history lessons, a curriculum fight that will shape what millions of Texas students — and likely students in other states — are taught.

title: Top two in Democratic gubernatorial straw poll highlight classic debate: Appeal to general electorate or the base?
why: Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez narrowly led a seven-way field in the state Democratic convention's gubernatorial straw poll, a result that crystallizes the party's strategic split between courting swing voters and energizing its progressive base ahead of 2026.

title: 14 Wounded In 'Horrific' Drive-By Mass Shooting In Roseland, Police Say
why: Two people in a red SUV opened fire on a crowd in Roseland, wounding 14 in what city data shows is Chicago's largest mass shooting of 2026 and intensifying scrutiny of summer gun violence on the South Side.

title: DOJ memo stokes fear among disability advocates of a return to institutionalization
why: A new Justice Department memo signals the federal government may pull back from enforcing the Olmstead mandate that keeps people with disabilities living in their communities, alarming advocates who warn it could unwind decades of progress nationwide.

title: How Fines of $1-Million-Plus May Pressure Immigrants to Self-Deport
why: The Department of Homeland Security is hitting immigrants with fines exceeding $1 million and hiring private debt collectors to pursue them, a financial-pressure campaign built to push people to "self-deport" rather than fight removal in court.

title: Inside the 'Mega Master' Hearings Reshaping New York's Immigration Courts
why: New York immigration courts have rolled out fast-tracked "mega master" hearings that process dozens of cases at once, a shift advocates say is steamrolling due process and accelerating deportations for asylum seekers.

title: Audit finds VA automation glitch ruined 98% of veteran survivors' benefits claims
why: A federal audit found a VA software defect wrongly mishandled about 98% of survivors' benefits claims filed by spouses and children of deceased veterans, an automation failure that cut families nationwide off from money they were owed.

title: 2 former Utah city employees face federal charges for allegedly helping someone evade ICE
why: Federal prosecutors charged two Logan court clerks who allegedly ushered three people out a courthouse back door as ICE agents waited out front, a striking move to criminally prosecute local public workers that could chill how court staff nationwide respond to immigration enforcement.

title: With subpoena, feds confirm a criminal investigation of Erin Stewart
why: A federal grand jury subpoena is the first official confirmation that prosecutors are investigating the former New Britain mayor over alleged misuse of a city credit card, tuition reimbursements and a charitable fund, putting a one-time GOP rising star in legal jeopardy.

title: Vermont student activist Mohsen Mahdawi faces new deportation order
why: An immigration judge ordered the Columbia activist and green-card holder removed to Jordan, escalating a closely watched test of whether the government can deport lawful permanent residents over pro-Palestinian speech. He has already filed an appeal.

title: In updated Helene funding request, Gov. Stein cuts back, focuses on 'significant gaps'
why: North Carolina's governor trimmed more than $3 billion from his Hurricane Helene recovery request, a pragmatic retreat that signals how much rebuilding storm-battered western counties may have to shoulder without Washington's help.

title: SpaceX land deal under fire with lawsuit by conservation groups
why: Conservation groups sued the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to block a land swap that would hand SpaceX habitat home to the endangered ocelot, forcing a public reckoning over whether a politically connected company can acquire protected federal land.

title: Minnesota psychiatric facility for youth ordered to close after a history of violations
why: State regulators moved to shut a youth psychiatric program after concluding it could not ensure children's safety, a rare forced closure that exposes oversight gaps at facilities housing some of Minnesota's most vulnerable kids.

title: Political reviews are causing a huge grant backlog at the National Park Service
why: Hundreds of millions of dollars in already-approved park funding is frozen at the Interior Department awaiting political vetting, stalling maintenance and conservation work at national parks across the country.

title: Did Donald Trump's signature 2025 legislation cut Medicaid spending by $1 trillion over a decade?
why: The fact-check confirms the megabill's roughly $1 trillion Medicaid cut and a new 80-hour-a-month work requirement, changes that will reshape who keeps health coverage for low-income residents in every state, not just Wisconsin.

title: What federal cuts to science funding could mean for the Great Lakes
why: A proposed federal budget would zero out the programs that underpin Great Lakes weather forecasting, water-quality monitoring and maritime safety, threatening the data tens of millions of people across eight states depend on.

title: Here's what Colorado should know about New World screwworm
why: Colorado officials are bracing for the flesh-eating New World screwworm to spread north from sightings in Texas and New Mexico, a livestock and public-health threat that is fast becoming a multistate story across the West.

title: Family of 3-year-old killed by car was under DCF investigation
why: A 3-year-old struck and killed in Manchester had been the subject of two prior reports to Connecticut's child-welfare agency, raising fresh questions about whether DCF's screening missed warning signs as the legislature debates a major overhaul of the department.

title: Santa Clara County and California sue to block ICE detention facility near Gilroy
why: After San José Spotlight obtained 111 pages of blueprints showing a 7,200-acre ICE detention center planned on agricultural land near Gilroy, Santa Clara County and AG Rob Bonta sued ICE and DHS — a test case other localities are watching as the administration races to expand detention capacity.

title: Greg Abbott recommends a crackdown on the data center industry
why: Gov. Abbott urged new regulation and a rethink of sales-tax breaks for data centers as the power-hungry facilities strain Texas's grid and water — a striking turn from a deregulation-first governor that signals how fast the data-center backlash is spreading to red states.

title: Mississippi Today pushes to unseal court filings in Greenville missing-DNA-evidence case
why: More than 100 pieces of DNA evidence vanished in a Greenville case, and Mississippi Today is fighting in court to unseal the filings — a transparency push that bears directly on whether convictions built on that evidence can stand.

title: Two Nashville charter schools cut classes for low enrollment
why: Two Nashville charters will eliminate fifth grade next year as underenrollment bites — an early sign of the demographic and funding pressures squeezing the charter sector that helped reshape urban education over the past two decades.

title: Denver-area inflation jumps to 5% — blame energy costs
why: Metro Denver prices rose 5% over the year as energy costs surged 15% since March and gasoline climbed 41.8% — a concrete measure of the cost-of-living squeeze driving Colorado's politics in an election year.

title: 15 big takeaways from Nevada's 2026 primary elections
why: Nevada voters set November's marquee matchups — Cannizzaro won the Democratic AG nod, Benitez-Thompson and Col. David Flippo took contested U.S. House primaries, and the secretary of state race stayed knife-edge — shaping control of a battleground state's election machinery.

title: Ten years on, still no memorial for the Pulse nightclub victims
why: As the 10th anniversary of the Pulse massacre nears, survivors and families still have no memorial — and the CPI found Orlando released only incomplete records on the millions raised, spending $262,000 repairing the building before demolishing it without accounting for donor funds.

title: It's the end of an era at the Arthur Street Hotel. Can the homeless-services nonprofit survive?
why: One of Louisville's signature low-barrier homeless shelters is closing in its current form, and advocates are scrambling to keep the nonprofit alive — a stress test of the safety net as cities nationwide pull back on hotel-based shelter models.

title: The city spent millions on a flailing domestic violence program no one asked for, advocates say
why: Amid a deadly surge in domestic violence, Chicago poured millions into a police-run program advocates say victims never requested and that has failed to launch — money that frontline shelters and survivor services say they desperately needed instead.

title: Ohio voters reject school levies, tax hikes around the state
why: Only 24 of 66 local school tax measures passed as Ohio voters rejected most levies, deepening a funding crisis for K-12 districts statewide and signaling growing tax fatigue that mirrors school-funding battles across the country.

title: Election Day live updates: Secretary of state’s office erroneously releases primary results
why: Files containing roughly 65,000 votes from rural counties and Washoe County were pushed to The Nevada Independent’s server hours before polls closed, then pulled — an election-administration stumble that raises questions about Nevada’s results-handling safeguards.

title: New Britain revokes Erin Stewart’s pension, demands money back
why: New Britain is clawing back $241,560 from former Mayor Erin Stewart for tuition reimbursements, severance and investigation costs, alleging she improperly boosted her own pay over 12 years running city hall — a rare municipal move to recover money from a departed official.

title: More than 100 people apply to be Charlotte’s next mayor
why: 103 people applied to finish departing Mayor Vi Lyles’ term, leaving the City Council — not voters — to appoint Charlotte’s next mayor through a public hearing process, an unusual democratic test for the nation’s 14th-largest city.

title: Read The Full Transcripts From The Controversial ‘Broadview 6’ Grand Jury Proceedings
why: Block Club published the full grand jury transcripts in the contested ‘Broadview 6’ case, giving the public an unfiltered look at proceedings that critics say were flawed — a transparency move in a closely watched criminal justice fight.

title: New pro-Talarico super PAC courts GOP voters in Senate race
why: A bipartisan group of federal campaign operatives launched a super PAC backing Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico and openly courting Republican voters, an early sign of how much outside money will flood one of 2026’s marquee Senate contests.

title: Record June heat wave creates pollution, health effects in Minnesota
why: June 9 marked the Twin Cities’ seventh straight 90-degree day, a record-breaking early heat wave driving up pollution and heat-related illness — with outdoor workers and lower-income communities, who often lack air conditioning, bearing the brunt.

title: Wyoming schools superintendent race features two primaries and five candidates
why: Five candidates across two primaries are vying to run Wyoming’s schools, a contest that will shape state policy on curriculum, school choice and book access for every Wyoming student amid intensifying culture-war fights over public education.

title: Pleading for routine purchases: Inside the chaos at the Forest Service in Vermont
why: Hundreds of pages of records VTDigger obtained show Trump-era budget freezes left U.S. Forest Service staff in Vermont begging for approval on routine purchases, stalling research and conservation work — a window into how federal cutbacks hit the ground in every state.

title: First came the robots. Then came the cameras. That’s when this Colorado mountain town had enough.
why: After surveillance cameras quietly appeared on poles around town hall, the water plant and the park, the small town of Paonia erupted into political turmoil and threats — a cautionary tale of unchecked municipal surveillance now playing out in towns nationwide.

title: Charlotte City Council approves 150-day data center moratorium
why: Charlotte’s council voted unanimously to pause new data centers for 150 days, the latest local government — from Texas to Missouri — to hit the brakes on a development wave straining power, water and neighborhoods.

title: Minnesota home seller goes on trial for allegedly preying on Muslim homebuyers
why: A broker who sold 160 homes through contract-for-deed deals — marketed as Sharia-compliant but allegedly overpriced and stripped of consumer protections — finally faced trial, four years after a Sahan Journal/ProPublica investigation exposed the practice.

title: GEO Group sues Colorado to block new immigrant-detention inspection law
why: The country’s largest private-prison contractor is suing to stop Colorado from running health and safety inspections at immigrant-detention facilities, testing whether states can oversee conditions inside federally contracted lockups.

title: Nashville mayor defends immigrant-rights coalition funding amid GOP scrutiny
why: Mayor Freddie O’Connell defended a $735,000 budget allocation to the Tennessee Immigrant and Refugee Rights Coalition, calling it years old as immigrant-services funding becomes a flashpoint in cities under a federal crackdown.

title: Federal judge strikes down Trump’s $100K visa fee for skilled foreign workers
why: A Massachusetts judge called the administration’s $100,000 visa fee an unlawful tax in a suit brought by 20 states, a ruling that immediately changes the math for employers and high-skill immigrants across the country.

title: Cigna to exit Colorado’s individual insurance market, forcing 40,000 to find new coverage
why: More than 40,000 Coloradans must shop for a new health insurer in 2027 after Cigna pulls out of the individual market nationwide, a sign of mounting instability in the marketplaces covering self-employed and gig workers.

title: Vermont readies fee hikes to visit state parks and public lands
why: State officials are moving to charge more for access to Vermont’s parks and recreation sites under a rule that lets the commissioner raise prices based on demand, shifting the cost of maintaining public lands onto the people who use them.

title: Imperial Beach elementary school closes as budget cuts and falling enrollment hit San Diego County
why: Central Elementary shut its doors amid budget shortfalls and declining enrollment, a closure echoing across San Diego County districts and a warning for public schools facing demographic and fiscal squeezes statewide.

title: A data center boom is coming to Texas. See where they’re going.
why: A Texas Tribune analysis maps at least 248 proposed data centers and warns the buildout could spike ordinary Texans’ electric bills and strain a grid already prone to failure — a fight now spreading to statehouses and county commissions nationwide.

title: Connecticut housing vouchers funnel families into segregated neighborhoods, study finds
why: A new study finds Connecticut’s rent vouchers steer recipients into racially and economically segregated areas, undercutting a program meant to widen housing choice — a failure documented in voucher systems across the U.S.

title: City worker who improved bike infrastructure killed while biking in Bridgeport
why: A Chicago transportation worker who spent his career building safer bike lanes was struck and killed while riding in Bridgeport, a death that underscores how far the city's street-safety goals remain from reality. Advocates are pointing to the loss as evidence the city must accelerate, not stall, its protected-bike-lane plans.

title: How West Virginians changed their state senator's mind on data centers
why: State Sen. Joey Garcia backed a law that supercharged data-center development, then reversed himself after constituents and his own research showed the projects drain water, raise power bills and strip away local control. His reversal — and the bill he now can't get a hearing for — is a case study other states are confronting as the AI build-out collides with rural communities.

title: Dozens gather in Charlotte to oppose planned ICE detention expansion in NC
why: Protesters rallied outside Charlotte's federal courthouse against plans to open three ICE detention centers in North Carolina, part of a national push to expand detention capacity. The fight over where and whether to site new facilities is playing out in communities across the country.

title: Winter storm response probe; Nashville Zoo opposes data center
why: A Metro commission wrapped its probe into Nashville Electric Service's faltering communication during January's winter storm, while the Nashville Zoo joined the growing list of institutions fighting a nearby data center. Both stories track how utilities and big-tech infrastructure are straining local accountability.

title: SoFi Stadium workers vote to authorize a strike days before the World Cup kicks off in LA
why: Concessions and hospitality workers at SoFi Stadium authorized a strike just days before Los Angeles hosts its first World Cup matches, giving the union maximum leverage over wages and staffing during a global event. A walkout would test how host cities handle labor disputes at the biggest sporting event in the country.

title: What the June 2 primary results tell us about politics in Montana
why: With Montana's longtime senator and congressman both stepping aside, their hand-picked successors swept the GOP primaries, signaling how firmly the party establishment still controls the state's open seats. The takeaways preview a competitive Western House race that could help decide control of Congress.

title: Second screwworm case in Texas confirmed as Abbott expands state disaster declaration
why: A second New World screwworm case was confirmed in a one-month-old calf in Zavala County just hours after Gov. Greg Abbott expanded a statewide disaster declaration, marking the flesh-eating parasite's first foothold inside Texas. A wider outbreak could devastate the cattle industry and force costly quarantines across the South and Southwest.

title: 'I am truly horrified that these conditions exist anywhere in the county'
why: Part of Charlottesville Tomorrow's 'No Way Out' series, this report documents squalid rental conditions tenants can't escape because Virginia's landlord-tenant law gives them little leverage to force repairs. It shows how weak habitability enforcement traps low-income renters — a gap mirrored in many states.

title: Texas county rescinds data center moratorium after $100 million lawsuit
why: Hill County commissioners unanimously repealed what may have been Texas's first data-center moratorium just two weeks after passing it, backing down when a developer sued for $100 million in damages. The retreat shows how the threat of litigation can override local efforts to slow the data-center rush.

title: EPA, conservation groups: Wyoming's 'impaired' water protocols run afoul of the Clean Water Act
why: Even the EPA and conservation groups say Wyoming's method for deciding which streams count as polluted violates the Clean Water Act, potentially leaving contaminated waterways off the cleanup list. How the state classifies impaired water determines which rivers get protected — a fight with stakes for downstream users across the West.

title: EPISD board approves plan to cut jobs by 8% or more, cutting $40 million in payroll
why: El Paso's largest school district declared financial exigency and approved cutting at least 8% of its workforce — roughly $40 million in payroll — to close a $47.9 million deficit, with the losses falling hardest on the women who make up two-thirds of its educators. It is an early look at the budget reckoning facing shrinking urban districts nationwide as enrollment and federal aid decline.

title: Dubbing June ‘Fidelity Month,’ Gov. Cox continues rightward shift away from being first to recognize Pride
why: Utah Gov. Spencer Cox — once the first Utah governor to recognize Pride Month — instead proclaimed June ‘Fidelity Month,’ a pointed symbol of how Republican officials are recalibrating on LGBTQ issues. The move signals where culture-war politics in statehouses may head heading into the midterms.

title: Wyoming GOP sues state, challenges constitutionality of ban on pre-primary candidate endorsements
why: The Wyoming Republican Party is asking a federal court to strike down a state law barring parties from financially backing one primary candidate over another, arguing it violates their speech rights. A victory would let party leaders steer primaries directly — a model other state parties are watching closely.

title: Kevin O’Leary to scale back Utah project — says it won’t be ‘the largest data center in the world’
why: Celebrity investor Kevin O'Leary said he will cut thousands of acres from his planned Box Elder County data-center campus after Gov. Cox publicly balked at its scale and water demands. The retreat shows local resistance reshaping the AI build-out even in business-friendly red states.

title: Ohio GOP senator called cops seeking charges against progressive blogger
why: A Republican state senator personally asked his local police chief to file harassment charges against the founder of a progressive newsletter that needles Ohio's GOP establishment, leading to the blogger's arrest at the Statehouse. The episode raises sharp First Amendment questions about lawmakers turning police power on their critics.

title: Colorado appeals court reverses convictions of 2 former Aurora paramedics in 2019 death of Elijah McClain
why: The Colorado Court of Appeals threw out the homicide convictions of the two Aurora paramedics who injected Elijah McClain with a fatal dose of ketamine and ordered new trials, reopening one of the cases that reshaped national scrutiny of police and EMS sedation. How the retrials proceed will shape whether prosecutors elsewhere can hold medics criminally liable in in-custody deaths.

title: Xcel Energy customers may be hit with the largest electric rate increase ever
why: A proposed settlement would grant Xcel its largest-ever electric rate hike — $225 million, adding about $6 to the average monthly bill — over consumer advocates' objections. With utilities nationwide seeking record increases to fund grid upgrades and data-center demand, the Colorado fight is a bellwether for household energy costs.

title: Blueprints confirm ICE involvement in South County facility
why: Leaked blueprints show a planned facility outside Gilroy is designed as a full ICE detention center — with detainee processing, holding cells, rooms for mothers with infants and weapons storage — undercutting officials' assurances about its purpose. The documents hand Santa Clara County residents concrete evidence as they fight to block the project.

title: Can CT make big debt payments while boosting towns, services?
why: Connecticut's bond-driven budget caps lock in large debt payments through 2028, squeezing what the state can spend on schools and town aid even as it runs surpluses. The tension between paying down debt and funding local services mirrors fiscal fights now playing out in statehouses across the country.

title: Louisville police reform effort under scrutiny after recent fatal shootings
why: Louisville's voluntary police-reform program faces fresh doubts after officers shot and killed two people experiencing mental-health crises in separate incidents. Five years after Breonna Taylor's death, the cases test whether the city's overhaul is actually changing how police respond to people in crisis.

title: Bird flu found at a northern Utah dairy: What you should know
why: Bird flu has resurfaced at a Cache County dairy, Utah's first confirmed case in cattle since early 2025, prompting weekly testing across northern Utah herds. Each new dairy outbreak raises the stakes for the milk supply, farmworker health and the risk of the virus adapting to spread more easily.

title: Surry County enacts 60-day data center development moratorium
why: Surry County froze new data center approvals for 60 days as residents push back on the power- and water-hungry projects. It joins a fast-growing wave of local moratoriums as the AI build-out collides with small communities from North Carolina to the Mountain West.

title: First U.S. screwworm case confirmed in South Texas
why: The USDA confirmed the first New World screwworm case on the U.S. side of the border, a flesh-eating parasite that menaces Texas' multibillion-dollar cattle industry. Containment failures here could ripple through the national beef supply and force costly eradication across the Southwest.

title: Judge Cheryl Blackburn's competency questioned in unsealed filings
why: Court documents unsealed by order of the Tennessee Supreme Court detail concerns about veteran Nashville judge Cheryl Blackburn's fitness to serve. The case exposes how the justice system handles a sitting judge whose capacity is in doubt while she continues to decide cases affecting defendants' liberty.

title: Lamont orders $300 grocery gift cards for residents losing SNAP
why: Gov. Ned Lamont is sending $300 grocery gift cards to an estimated 25,000 Connecticut residents cut off from federal food aid under new SNAP work rules. It's a costly state stopgap other governors are watching as the same federal cuts push families off benefits nationwide.

title: Woman killed at busy NW Side intersection where planned traffic light was never installed
why: A 62-year-old Skokie mother of three was struck and killed crossing a Northwest Side intersection where the city promised a traffic signal for years but never installed one. The death puts a human cost on the bureaucratic delays that leave pedestrians exposed on neighborhood streets.

title: How the US Supreme Court's Callais ruling erased a key Mississippi voting rights victory
why: A US Supreme Court decision in Callais wiped out a hard-won ruling that would have forced special elections for Mississippi Supreme Court districts drawn to dilute Black votes, ending Black Mississippians' best near-term shot at fairer representation on the state's high court. The reasoning reaches far beyond Mississippi, narrowing how the Voting Rights Act can challenge racially skewed maps nationwide.

title: Ex-sheriff's deputy banned from police work over 'trading cards' of suspects
why: A Vermont oversight panel permanently barred a former Lamoille County deputy from policing after he turned arrestees' booking photos into mocking 'trading cards.' The rare decertification is a concrete test of whether states will strip badges over conduct that degrades the people officers arrest.

title: Louisville mayor backs inspector general in dispute with police union
why: Mayor Craig Greenberg said he won't shut down the Office of Inspector General's investigations into police misconduct, siding with independent oversight against the police union. The standoff mirrors fights in cities nationwide over who gets to scrutinize the police.

title: After a grim ski season, drought is crippling Colorado's rafting season
why: Record-low river flows after a dismal snow year are gutting Colorado's commercial rafting season and the outfitters who depend on snowmelt. It's an early, tangible economic warning of the deepening water crisis squeezing the entire Western U.S.

title: What we know about Montana's 2026 primary election results
why: Montana voters chose nominees June 2 in primaries setting the field for a U.S. Senate seat, U.S. House districts, two Public Service Commission spots and roughly 40 legislative races riven by Republican infighting. The outcomes shape control of a swing-state delegation heading into November.

title: EPISD poised to declare financial emergency, eliminate hundreds of jobs to close massive budget gap
why: El Paso ISD trustees were briefed June 2 on a plan to declare financial exigency and cut hundreds of jobs to erase a $42 million deficit for 2026-27; a Thursday vote could let the superintendent break employee contracts. Falling enrollment is forcing the same wrenching choice on districts nationwide.

title: US Education Secretary Linda McMahon tours Essex tech center, prompting protest
why: Education Secretary Linda McMahon's June 2 stop at a Vermont career-tech center drew dozens of student and community protesters as she promoted her 'Returning Education to the States' push to shrink the federal role. The visit previews a national fight over dismantling the Education Department.

title: Reacting to Supreme Court, NC House wants to limit tourism occupancy tax spending
why: Responding to a state Supreme Court ruling, NC House members advanced a bill June 2 to bar counties from spending hotel occupancy taxes on public safety and core services, targeting Currituck County's use of the money. It tests how tourism-reliant counties can fund basic services.

title: Thousands to lose Medi-Cal and food aid in Santa Clara County
why: New federal work requirements that took effect June 1 now reach adults up to age 64; UC Berkeley estimates 129,000 Santa Clara County residents will lose Medi-Cal by 2028, with CalFresh recipients also exposed. The same One Big Beautiful Bill Act rules are squeezing safety-net families in every AJP region.

title: Colorado officials call for more state actions to combat impacts of drought
why: Members of Colorado's Drought Task Force urged Gov. Jared Polis on June 2 to issue an emergency proclamation to unlock aid as worsening drought grips the state. With record-early snowmelt across the West, the plea signals how strained water and wildfire conditions are becoming region-wide.

title: Metro's Gallatin Pike plans paused for Choose How You Move
why: Nashville officials drew backlash June 2 after pausing safety redesigns for Main Street and Gallatin Pike, two of the city's deadliest corridors, under its Choose How You Move program. Advocates say the delay leaves pedestrians exposed on roads with a history of fatal crashes.

title: Missouri's drive to eliminate income tax leaves KC-area officials with more questions than answers
why: Missouri's push to phase out its income tax leaves Kansas City-area officials unsure how to backfill the services that depend on state revenue, the Beacon reported June 2. Several states are racing to scrap income taxes, and the local fallout here is a preview for all of them.

title: Progressive blogger arrested outside Ohio statehouse
why: DJ Byrnes, founder of the progressive blog The Rooster, was arrested at the Ohio Statehouse and charged with telecommunications harassment over messages to a state senator he routinely mocks, in a story updated June 2. Free-speech advocates warn the case could signal officials punishing political criticism.

title: As Ned Lamont touts record, Josh Elliott's campaign strengthens
why: Challenger Josh Elliott cleared the fundraising threshold to qualify for a $3.75 million public grant, sharpening his Democratic primary fight with Gov. Ned Lamont, CT Mirror reported June 2. The race tests whether a well-funded progressive can pull an incumbent governor leftward.

title: Federal judge blocks breakup of NCAR in Boulder, blasting Trump for political revenge on Colorado
why: A judge halted the administration's plan to dismantle Boulder's National Center for Atmospheric Research and hand its supercomputer to the University of Wyoming, calling it retaliation against Colorado. A test of how far courts will check federal payback against blue states.

title: Federal prosecutors tout results of Charlotte crime crackdown
why: Prosecutors charged 56 people and arrested 157 fugitives in a three-month Charlotte surge dubbed Operation Spring Cleaning. The crackdown reflects the Justice Department's expanding use of federal charges to drive local policing.

title: Ohio property tax overhaul signed into law, cutting taxes by billions
why: Gov. DeWine signed bills capping the automatic property-tax increases that come from rising home values, cutting expected future taxes by as much as $3 billion. Relief for homeowners that also squeezes the schools and local services funded by those dollars.

title: Texas lifts ban on CDLs for temporary agriculture workers, drops Spanish-language test option
why: Texas DPS lifted its ban on commercial driver's licenses for immigrants on temporary farm-work visas while scrapping the Spanish-language CDL test, two moves that reshape who can legally drive trucks in the state's economy.

title: Questions about El Paso ISD's financial crisis answered
why: El Paso ISD expects a $52.8 million deficit and may cut about 410 jobs by declaring financial exigency, a rare step that lets a district break employee contracts. Falling enrollment is forcing the same reckoning on school systems across the country.

title: Whistleblower phones were 'blowing up' in Utah state auditor's office after MIDA data center vote, official says
why: A flood of whistleblower tips hit Utah's state auditor after a state board fast-tracked a sprawling Box Elder County data center, the Tribune reports. A window into how officials are greenlighting power-hungry data projects with little public scrutiny.

title: Debate over ICE masking bill complicates, for a moment, end of session in the Vermont House
why: A measure to bar immigration agents from concealing their identities nearly derailed the close of Vermont's legislative session, part of a growing wave of states trying to force transparency on masked federal ICE officers.

title: New York's brand-new casino is in a $500M+ fight with the state
why: Resorts World, New York's newest casino, is pushing legislation to escape more than $500 million in payments owed to the horse-racing industry. A high-stakes fight over who profits from the state's gambling expansion.

title: The USDA canceled $300M in farm grants, citing fraud. Did it make up the evidence?
why: The USDA terminated 49 of 50 grantees in a $300 million land-access program for fraud, but Grist found the agency's evidence appears thin and in places invented. Hundreds of farmers, many of them Black and first-generation, lost funding they were promised.

title: All eyes on Lamont as CT's hunger crisis worsens
why: As federal SNAP cuts take hold and grocery prices climb, Connecticut food banks are stretched thin and advocates say Gov. Lamont has been slow to act. A preview of the hunger squeeze hitting low-income families in every state.

title: Lummis family could cash in on Microsoft data center expansion through Cheyenne land sales
why: Sen. Cynthia Lummis and her relatives own roughly 6,000 acres ringing Microsoft's Cheyenne data center — the same company that bought their land in 2021 — even as she sponsors crypto and AI bills and collects tech-PAC money. A textbook conflict-of-interest story riding the national data-center land rush.

title: Vermont Legislature passes landmark education reform without forcing districts to merge
why: After a session consumed by the fight, lawmakers passed a sweeping overhaul that swaps mandatory school-district consolidation for voluntary mergers — reshaping how Vermont funds and governs its schools without the forced closures many towns feared.

title: El Paso ISD delays financial exigency vote as district prepares for possible layoffs
why: EPISD postponed a vote on declaring financial exigency that could cut 410 jobs to close a $42 million gap, with the superintendent expecting the workforce to shrink about 10% over the summer. Falling enrollment is forcing the same reckoning on districts nationwide.

title: What's in the 2026 NY State Budget? Here's What To Know.
why: New York's $269 billion budget rolls back the centerpiece of the state's landmark climate law, bans local contracts to detain people for ICE, and leaves an estimated 450,000 people set to lose Essential Plan coverage in July without a fix.

title: ICE agent who shot migrant in Minnesota arrested in Texas
why: Texas Rangers and federal agents arrested ICE officer Christian Castro on five counts, including filing a false report, over his shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant in Minneapolis. Rare criminal accountability for a federal agent during the deportation surge.

title: Kentucky judge issues arrest warrant for former Gov. Matt Bevin, who blames 'boulder' for not appearing
why: A judge ordered the arrest of former Gov. Matt Bevin after he again skipped a court hearing, telling the court by video that 'a very large boulder' through the back of his house kept him away. A former official facing the same enforcement as any other defendant.

title: Montana state Senate calls on Jonathan Windy Boy to resign
why: At least 39 of 50 state senators signed a bipartisan letter urging the long-serving Democrat to resign over allegations he sent sexually explicit messages to underage girls in 2002 and harassed a fellow lawmaker, calling the conduct 'disqualifying for anyone holding public office.'

title: Lt. Gov. Randy McNally punishes Democratic senators
why: Tennessee's lieutenant governor stripped committee seats and cut reimbursements for Democratic senators who protested during the redistricting special session — retaliation that tests how far legislative leaders can punish dissenting members.

title: E-Bikes, Scooters Face New Age And Speed Limits Under Bill Approved By Legislators
why: Illinois lawmakers approved the state's first 'micromobility' rules — age requirements, speed caps and limits on where e-bikes and scooters can operate — as cities scramble to regulate a fast-growing and largely unmanaged form of transport.

title: In effort to boost hiring, short-staffed NC prisons are letting people start early
why: North Carolina's new pilot lets correctional officers begin work before their background checks are finished — a safety gamble driven by chronic understaffing that prison systems across the country are confronting.

title: Speakers at public hearing mostly in favor of data center moratorium in Charlotte
why: At a raucous Charlotte City Council hearing, residents lined up to back a 150-day pause on new data centers, citing strain on power and water. Pair it with Utah's ballot fight and Wyoming's grid worries and a clear pattern emerges: the local backlash against hyperscale data centers has gone national.

title: Mamdani Kills Adams-Era Charter Commission and Starts His Own COGE
why: Mayor Zohran Mamdani dissolved the charter commission seated in Eric Adams's final hours and launched his own Commission on Government Efficiency — a pointed nod to Trump's DOGE — to rewrite how city government runs. How NYC's new administration reshapes the charter will set a template for big-city progressive governance.

title: Caesars to be acquired by Fertitta Entertainment in a $17.6B transaction
why: Tilman Fertitta's $17.6 billion all-cash deal would take the largest U.S. casino company private and likely force property sales to clear antitrust review, reshaping ownership across the Las Vegas Strip and regional gaming markets. The deal touches tens of thousands of casino jobs and the tax base of every Nevada gaming town.

title: Texas' newest prison book ban curbs hardback, used texts
why: A new Texas prison policy bars incarcerated people from receiving hardback and used books; officials cite contraband while advocates say it sharply expands an already-large banned-books list. Prison reading restrictions are spreading across state corrections systems, and Texas, with one of the nation's largest prison populations, sets the bar.

title: News outlets sue Penn State trustees over speech limits
why: Spotlight PA, the Centre Daily Times and StateCollege.com sued Penn State trustee leaders in federal court, arguing a bylaw 'gag policy' that bars trustees from publicly criticizing the board violates the First Amendment. A ruling would set precedent for how public-university boards nationwide can silence dissenting members and limit press access.

title: Gross Dam injunction heads back to court after talks stall
why: The fight over Denver Water's $600 million Gross Reservoir expansion returns to federal appeals court in July after settlement talks collapsed, leaving the half-built project in legal limbo. The case is a marquee test of how far environmental law can halt major Western water infrastructure already under construction.

title: Box Elder County to decide Thursday if Utahns can vote on data center decision
why: Box Elder County commissioners weighed Thursday whether to let voters decide the fate of a massive hyperscale data-center campus — a direct-democracy fight over a project opponents have lawyered up to stop. As communities from Utah to Charlotte to Wyoming move to slow data-center buildout, putting it on the ballot is the new front line.

title: Detainee suicides soar under Trump; MNPD revives a cold case
why: Deaths in immigration detention have climbed sharply during the administration's deportation surge, and the Banner ties the national trend to Nashville's own ICE pipeline as local police reopen a cold case. Detention-death counts are the metric that drives oversight hearings and lawsuits, and the story will resonate in every city absorbing expanded ICE operations.

title: Texas' discipline push sends kids to 'jail-like' campuses
why: Texas lawmakers are steering more students into disciplinary alternative education programs that critics describe as jail-like, pulling kids out of regular classrooms over behavior. As states nationwide tighten school discipline after pandemic-era disruptions, Texas' expansion is a template other legislatures will study — and a warning about who gets pushed out.

title: 'They Put Me In a Cell': Old-Timers Fight Eviction From the New Times Square
why: A landlord converting a Hell's Kitchen SRO into a Times Square hotel allegedly tore out staircases and shared bathrooms to force out rent-stabilized tenants like 59-year-old Garratt Kennedy, who'd lived there 25 years. The piece documents the eviction tactics displacing long-term low-income renters as tourist-zone redevelopment accelerates.

title: Partial repeal of Vermont’s land-use law Act 181 heads to Gov. Phil Scott’s desk
why: After a 28-2 Senate vote, Vermont is sending Gov. Phil Scott a partial rollback of Act 181 — the landmark 2024 land-use overhaul meant to channel growth into already-developed areas. The retreat, less than two years after enactment, is a marquee data point for how hard it is to hold the line on growth-control statutes when housing pressure spikes, and other small-state legislatures (NH, ME, RI) will read this closely.

title: Gov. Bill Lee urged to halt Tennessee death penalty after botched IV attempt
why: Attorneys for Tony Carruthers are pressing Gov. Bill Lee to pause Tennessee’s death penalty after executioners failed to place IV lines for his lethal injection earlier this month.
